problem: VLN agents are trained and evaluated on a single instruction granularity (fine-grained R2R/RxR or coarse REVERIE/SOON), so their robustness to realistic, partially specified instructions of varying detail is unknown, and they degrade when instructions are underspecified.
motivation: Real users give short, underspecified commands rather than step-by-step route descriptions, especially in familiar environments. Agents trained on one granularity degrade on another, and underspecified text causes temporal reference misalignment between sub-instructions and visual transitions, calling for granularity-aware grounding and exploration.
key_idea: Introduce the ULN setting with the multi-level R2R-ULN benchmark, and handle it with an instruction classifier, granularity-specific sub-networks (GSS) for low-/high-level instructions, and an uncertainty-triggered multi-step lookahead exploration module (E2E).
insight: Training on a single granularity or a mix of R2R and R2R-last gives a compromised result, while swapping only one critical sub-network (text encoder for VLN-BERT, cross-modal transformer for HAMT) yields high-level gains cheaply. The ablation shows GSS gives +5.1 SR on L3, lookahead gives +1-2 SR on all levels, and state freeze adds a complementary gain on L3. Early exploration matters, since the agent deviates from the teacher almost every step after the third correction, so errors compound.
method: Instruction classification: embedding + average pooling + FC binary classifier routes each instruction to low-level (L0-L2) or high-level (L3); ~85% accuracy.

Granularity Specific Sub-networks (GSS): find the sub-network (f_text, f_img, f_hist, f_cm) whose replacement from a high-level-trained agent (trained on last sentence of R2R) gives the largest L3 gain; retrain it from scratch with the rest frozen (text encoder for VLN-BERT, cross-modal transformer for HAMT), adding 25-38% parameters.

Uncertainty estimation: a two-layer MLP on concatenated last-layer vision-to-text attention and action logits outputs a grounding uncertainty score in [0,1]; labels come from disagreement with the teacher action on pseudo-underspecified instructions created by randomly dropping sub-instructions (chunking).

Multi-step lookahead: when uncertainty > 0.5 (at most 3 times per episode), simulate K=1 greedy steps ahead for the top-C candidate actions with the trained agent as explorer, and re-score actions with beta_t,c plus a gamma-weighted (1.2) sum of future max logits.
State freeze: during lookahead, reuse history state h_{t-1} rather than h_t to keep attention on the pending sub-instruction until alignment recovers.

R2R-ULN dataset: MTurk workers progressively simplify R2R val instructions into L1 (redundancy removed), L2 (sub-instructions dropped), L3 (one-sentence goal description); 3132 val-seen / 6714 val-unseen / 4198 test instructions.

setting.backbone: VLN-BERT and HAMT (trained on R2R + R2R-last, with GSS sub-network, classifier, and uncertainty MLP)
setting.training_data: R2R train (full instructions) plus R2R-last (last sentences of R2R instructions) only; no R2R-ULN training; pseudo-underspecified instructions via chunking for uncertainty training
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views with angle features (Matterport3D panoramas)
setting.privileged: none (ground-truth level class used only in an ablation of GSS without the classifier)

numbers.eval_set_note: 2k val-seen / 4.5k val-unseen subset sampled from the full R2R-ULN (30% L1, 70% L2, 100% L3); metrics averaged over L1-L3
numbers.extra: trained on R2R + R2R-last; E2E lookahead exploration (longer paths)

numbers_note: R2R-ULN is the paper's own benchmark, so its numbers are stored under 'other:R2R-ULN'. Main-table numbers are averages over L1-L3 on subsets; per-level SR is in Table 4 (e.g. VLN-BERT w/ E2E val-unseen L1/L2/L3 = 55.7/47.6/39.5). Table 7 ablation reports full val-unseen numbers that differ slightly.
results: On R2R-ULN val-unseen, GSS + E2E improves SR by about 10% relative over baselines (VLN-BERT 39.3 -> 44.7; HAMT 41.7 -> 44.6), with GSS alone giving +3.8 to +5 absolute SR on L3. E2E raises SR at the cost of SPL through longer paths. R2R performance is maintained without E2E.
limitations: English-only, indoor-only dataset; multilingual and outdoor underspecification are not covered.

E2E trades SPL for SR through much longer trajectories, and on R2R it can hurt (HAMT SR -1.8) due to inaccurate uncertainty estimation; the classifier is only ~85% accurate and hurts HAMT on short R2R instructions.
The setting is validation-only for the dataset (agents are trained on R2R only), and the main evaluation uses subsets.
